author: RosieCampbell
text:
Relatedly, I would like it if we could stop conflating:

- Consciousness (whether AI has subjective experience)

- Danger (whether AI has the capability or propensity to cause catastrophe)

- Moral patienthood (whether we have an ethical obligation to consider AI welfare)

text: Some people seem to have interpreted this thread as me trying to persuade people of my views, when in fact I'm trying to offer advice for how they can persuade me of theirs

quoted.text:
“It’s so sad to see people convinced of X”
“People who believe X are biased”
“It’s harmful to believe X”
“If X were true it would imply these bad things”
“These bad people believe X”

These may all be true, but unfortunately they have no bearing on whether X is in fact true

author: RosieCampbell
text:
If you are worried about catastrophic AGI risk:

Do you see for yourself how it could lead to doom, or are mostly trusting the judgement of people you respect on this? (If both, pick the first one)

author: RosieCampbell
text: @ciphergoth @daniel_filan To crystallize more: I think that the proponents who say "if you try it you'll see" think that the skeptics don't believe they will become convinced if they tried it and that's what's stopping them, whereas the point I'm making is that's not the issue

author: RosieCampbell
text:
Many responses to this question are of the form "try it, then you'll see".

Similarly, people tell me about wacky insights they've had through meditation and how I just need to try it.

Both have the flamingo problem!

quoted.text:
People who *genuinely* believe that DMT gives you access to a communication network between advanced beings... Why? What makes you feel so certain that those experiences aren't mere hallucinations?

I'm asking very earnestly. I'll seriously consider any argument/evidence. Thanks!

author: RosieCampbell
text: If there was a pill where 100% of people who take it become completely convinced that everyone is a flamingo, I can be sure that a) if I take it I too will believe everyone is a flamingo, and b) all those people are mistaken and it would be a mistake to take the flamingo pill.

author: RosieCampbell
text:
Gotta say I am very surprised by this so far! Assumed people would find the idea of AI "wanting" to cause catastrophe more far-fetched than it being able to. 

If a system is good at hacking and persuasion, seems like it could do a lot of damage pretty easily?

quoted.text:
If you don't think we need to worry about catastrophic risks from AGI, is it primarily because:

- It won't have the capability: AI will never be powerful enough to cause catastrophe

- It won't have the propensity: AI will never have reason to cause catastrophe

author: RosieCampbell
text: For people saying "something else", please comment! I'm struggling to think of reasons beyond it not being capable or having the propensity (if you think something like "humans will ultimately stay in control", I'd consider that a capability limitation)
